clue.text: Sample Breakfast Show on radio

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is spoken, so the word for the show is taken by its sound

parts.note: a serial is a broadcast show told in instalments

explanation.surface: A radio station previews its morning programme with a taste of what is on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breakfast Show' looks like one phrase, a radio programme; split it so that 'Sample Breakfast' is the definition and 'Show on radio' is a serial said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl of cornflakes or muesli is a typical example of what people eat in the morning.

clue.text: Unethical treatment of the Big N — after taking a turn — is integral to game

indicators.note: something integral to a thing is built into its middle, so these letters go inside the game

parts.note: SIM is short for a simulation game such as The Sims
the capital letter N given a quarter turn anticlockwise becomes a Z, which is what 'after taking a turn' asks
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint about how large people are treated, set against a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after taking a turn' rotates the letter N through ninety degrees, where it becomes Z; ZIS then goes into SIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Sizism is prejudice or discrimination against people because of their body size, here the large.

clue.text: Trader's advantage, except when index gets added

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, as in 'all bar one'
in maths an index is a power, so a number whose index is added to is gaining power

explanation.surface: A merchant's edge disappears unless a stock market index rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'index' looks like a financial index; in mathematics it is the exponent, or power, of a number.
explanation.definitionFit: The strength of one's position in a negotiation is exactly what lets a dealer drive a good price.

clue.text: Some maths: complex elaborating on it not necessary

indicators.note: complex here means intricately mixed up, so the letters of the word are rearranged
the letters of these two words are not needed, so they are removed from the jumbled pool

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A student finds a tricky mathematical topic needs no further explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges ELABORATING; 'not necessary' takes out the letters of ON IT, and the seven left spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is a branch of mathematics using letters for unknown numbers.

clue.text: Almost entirely digital hit Spears remastered as iPod No. 1?

indicators.note: a remastered recording is reworked, so the letters are rearranged
almost all of the word, with its final letter removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the full stop
the figure 1 looks like the letter I

explanation.surface: A digitally remastered Britney Spears single tops the iPod chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost entirely' drops the L of DIGITAL; DIGITA, AS, IPOD, NO and I are then 'remastered' into the title of a 2000 Britney Spears single.
explanation.definitionFit: This 2000 single was a major chart success for the pop singer Britney Spears.

clue.text: Branch mum caught in pedal

indicators.note: one word is trapped inside another, so these letters are placed within the other piece

parts.note: pedal as an adjective means of the foot
mum is a call for silence, as is sh

explanation.surface: A mother gets her foot stuck on a bicycle pedal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like a mother; it is the instruction to keep quiet ('mum's the word'). 'pedal' is read as the adjective, 'of foot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot growing off a main stem is a side branch, as is anything derived from a larger body.

clue.text: I am inclined to support young lady of Europa?

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits underneath, so these letters come after the other piece

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
taken as written
to lean is to be inclined, so 'I am inclined' is I lean

explanation.surface: A man offers to prop up a girl from the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Europa' looks like the continent or the woman of myth; it is one of the four moons of Jupiter that Galileo discovered, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Europa, Io, Ganymede and Callisto are named after Galileo, who first saw them through a telescope.

clue.text: The postman is Greendale's gossip, so … memorise everything!

definitions.text: The postman is Greendale's gossip, so
definitions.meaning: Postman Pat is the postman of Greendale in a British children's TV show; if he holds the village gossip, one learns the lot from him
to have something ... is to know it by heart

explanation.surface: A village postman knows all the local news, so learn it from him.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a children's TV series set in the fictional village of Greendale. Read as 'get it all off Pat', the phrase means hear all the news from him.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning a speech word for word, so that it can be recited perfectly, is having it off pat.

clue.text: See 8
Your doctor needs to take a break

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the letter goes within the other piece

parts.note: GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor in the UK

explanation.surface: A doctor is told to have a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a GP (general practitioner) is the family doctor most people see first.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap is an interval or pause, as a break in activity is.

clue.text: Boo this sweet when mentioning unexpected return

indicators.note: 'Boo this' means put boo with the answer; taking that boo away again leaves the sweet
mentioning means speaking, so the thrown stick is taken by its sound

parts.note: a boomerang comes back to the thrower, which surprises people who have not seen one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at a dessert when it is brought back to the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Say BOO followed by the answer and it sounds like BOOMERANG, a throwing stick that returns: remove the BOO and the sweet is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Meringue is a baked confection of whisked egg white and sugar, served as a dessert.

clue.text: Bird family to which swallow initially belongs

indicators.note: this word only joins the neighbouring pieces: it says which one stands next to which in the answer
initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to belong, or be part of, is read here as simply 'is'
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A bird watcher asks which family the swallow belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' looks like part of the bird theme; only its first letter is used. 'S is kin' says the S belongs to the family.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch of Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Largely plain priest enters key on very busy railroad

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the first piece comes next to the rest
the priest goes into the key, so these letters sit inside the island

parts.note: a key is a low island, and an ait is a small river island
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
red-hot means extremely active or in great demand
the El is the elevated railroad in Chicago

explanation.surface: A clergyman steps onto a crowded railway line in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the dish: food served this way comes with simple parsley butter, hence 'Largely plain'. 'key' is an island, not a lock or a piano key.
explanation.definitionFit: Food served this way comes with a simple parsley and lemon butter, so it is hardly dressed up.

clue.text: Husband is joining rock band

indicators.note: the husband joins the rock by going into it, so the letter sits inside

parts.note: aa is a rough type of volcanic lava rock

explanation.surface: A married man becomes a member of a rock group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock band' reads as one phrase; split it, with 'rock' giving AA (rough lava) and 'band' the definition, the Norwegian pop group A-ha.
explanation.definitionFit: A-ha are the Norwegian pop trio behind 'Take On Me'.

clue.text: Know-it-all is driving over limit

indicators.note: over signals turning the words back to front

parts.note: someone who is driving something in hard rams it
to tie is to restrict or limit

explanation.surface: A smug driver insists on going above the speed limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses the synonym of 'is driving'. 'driving over limit' looks like speeding, but 'driving' means forcing in hard, and 'limit' is a verb, to restrict.
explanation.definitionFit: A smartie, or smarty, is a clever-clogs who always has the answer.

clue.text: Chinese guy, bold almost to the end

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: the word runs almost to the end, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: daring means bold

explanation.surface: A Chinese man is brave nearly to the last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost to the end' drops the G of DARING.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is the main language of China, and once named a senior Chinese official.

clue.text: Brood having filled cabin #7, good news we hear from purser?

indicators.note: we hear marks a phrase taken only by its sound

parts.note: with cabin 7 taken, the purser can still announce happily that there is a room in the next cabin, number eight

explanation.surface: A passenger worries until the ship's officer confirms a berth is free.
explanation.walkthrough: A purser is the officer on a ship who allots cabins: 'room in eight' said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To brood is to dwell on something gloomily, turning it over in the mind.

clue.text: Press job excluded it in general cases

indicators.note: the cases of a word are its first and last letters, which enclose the rest

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for general

explanation.surface: A newspaper task is described as having dropped something in most instances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' takes the first and last letters of 'excluded', E and D; 'in general' looks like 'usually' but gives IN and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Preparing copy for publication by correcting and cutting it is work done on a newspaper.

clue.text: Diamond reserve

definitions.meaning: icy reserve means cool, unfriendly restraint

explanation.definitionFit: Criminals call gems ice, and a cold, distant manner can also be called that.

clue.text: Something of no value in trunk now neglected

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An old item stored in a trunk lies forgotten because it is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of no value' is not 'worthless': in an equation an unknown is a quantity whose value is not yet known.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra an unknown is a quantity, like x, whose value has yet to be found.

clue.text: Lacking ideas, where students go worshipping royals from birth

parts.note: uni is short for university
the Magi were the kings who came to worship the infant Jesus
a language spoken from birth is spoken natively

explanation.surface: A dull person thinks students spend their time adoring the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magi, or Three Kings, came to worship the newborn Jesus; 'from birth' looks like part of their story but gives NATIVELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Without imagination means showing no creativity or original thought.

clue.text: Expressed "five degrees above freezing" with a bigger zero?

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
the degree sign is a small raised circle; drawn as a bigger zero it becomes the letter O, as the clue's last words ask
iced means frozen

explanation.surface: A forecaster reports a temperature of five degrees above zero.
explanation.walkthrough: Write five degrees as V° and enlarge the degree sign into a full-sized O; then put it above ICED, read as 'freezing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice a view is to express it in words.

clue.text: Changing order for Whopper, a kind of beef product

indicators.note: the order of the parts is changed, so the second half moves to the front

parts.note: a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: A diner changes their fast-food order away from a burger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whopper' suggests the burger, but it means a big lie; swap BIG and LIE for Liebig, a meat extract named after the German chemist Justus von Liebig.
explanation.definitionFit: Liebig's Extract of Meat was a concentrated stock sold from the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Prison life punctuated by hanging at intervals

indicators.note: punctuated by means broken up by, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: bio is short for biography, a life story

indicators.note: at intervals takes every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A prisoner's life is interrupted by executions now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at intervals' picks the even letters of 'hanging', AGN, which go into BIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagnio was a Turkish or oriental prison for slaves.

clue.text: This may be revealing for one wearing new line: I say!

indicators.note: the one wearing new line has it around itself, so those letters go outside

parts.note: for one means for example, abbreviated eg
taken as written
gee is an exclamation of surprise, like 'I say!'

explanation.surface: Someone sees a woman in a skimpy new outfit and exclaims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This may be revealing' defines a flimsy nightdress; 'wearing' wraps N and L round EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a light, often sheer, nightgown or dressing gown that shows the body.

clue.text: Sixties rockers dodging the question

indicators.note: dodging means avoiding, so the named word is left out

parts.note: The ... were a British rock band of the 1960s
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rock band of the sixties avoids a reporter's question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodging the question' looks like a phrase; 'dodging the' drops THE from the band's name, leaving 'question' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Who is an interrogative word, asking about a person, so it introduces a query.

clue.text: "Truth hurts", so one's told

parts.note: because honesty would wound, a harmless untruth is spoken instead to spare feelings

explanation.surface: Someone is told a hard fact on the grounds that the truth hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fib told out of kindness avoids causing pain.

clue.text: See 27
